interpretation: the published benchmarking paper reports AUROC 0.86-0.98 for strategies that draw 3, 5 or 10 random points inside each landslide polygon. Half the polygons cover fewer than 10 cells of the 10 m factor grid, so most of those points read identical covariate values and random K-fold puts copies of one record on both sides of the split. The high scores measure duplicate memorisation, not skill.

published_reference.source: Samodra & Nugroho, doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-1441095/v1 (published as Artificial Intelligence in Geosciences, doi:10.1016/j.aiig.2024.100093)
